record.paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
record.original_question: Let X be a complex Banach space, T in L(X) a bounded operator, and Y = E_X(T) the linear subspace formed from the generalized kernels of lambda - T, equivalently the union of p(T)^{-1}(0) over all nonzero polynomials p. Let T'_Y : X/Y -> X/Y be the quotient operator induced by T. Is the point spectrum pi(T'_Y), meaning the set of lambda for which lambda - T'_Y is not injective, empty?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a complex Banach space and let $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$ be a bounded linear operator on $X$. Define
$$E_X(T) \;=\; \bigcup_{\lambda \in \mathbb{C}} \ker\!\big((\lambda I - T)^{\infty}\big) \;=\; \bigcup_{0 \neq p \in \mathbb{C}[z]} \ker p(T),$$
where $\ker((\lambda I - T)^\infty) = \bigcup_{n\geq 1} \ker((\lambda I - T)^n)$ is the generalized kernel of $\lambda I - T$. Set $Y = E_X(T)$, viewed as a (not necessarily closed) linear subspace of $X$ that is invariant under $T$. Let $\widetilde{Y}$ denote the closure of $Y$ in $X$, and let $T'_Y : X/\widetilde{Y} \to X/\widetilde{Y}$ denote the bounded quotient operator induced by $T$. The point spectrum of an operator $S$ is
$$\pi(S) \;=\; \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : \lambda I - S \text{ is not injective}\}.$$
Question: Is it true that $\pi(T'_Y) = \emptyset$ for every choice of complex Banach space $X$ and every $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$?
